chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Aasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no problem with drinking the grape juice for six days. Ibn Abi Umeyr said, 'Its meaning is, as long as it has not boiled.'

key_terms.الْعَصِيرِ: Fresh grape juice, specifically before fermentation
key_terms.سِتَّةَ أَيَّامٍ: Six days, the specified duration for permissibility
key_terms.يَغْلِ: It boils, indicating the condition of heating or boiling

ai.seo_question: How long can grape juice be consumed before it becomes impermissible or changes status in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the transitional period during which grape juice remains permissible (halal) before naturally fermenting into wine, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence regarding the prohibition of khamr. The condition 'ما لم يغل' (unless it boils) refers to the vigorous bubbling that signals the onset of fermentation, marking the precise moment the beverage becomes impure. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on natural processes and the gradual transformation of substances, distinguishing it from immediate intoxicants.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Aasim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is no problem with drinking the (grape) juice of six days (old)’. Ibn Abu Umeyr (the narrator) said, ‘Its meaning is, for as long as it was not boiled’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Muhammad ibn ‘Asem who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is not unlawful to drink juice (grape juice) up to six days.’ Ibn abu ‘Umayr has said, ‘It means that it does not become intoxicating liquor and unlawful before it comes to a boil.’”
